articles.title: The Full Twelve Rounds
articles.description: Ada Wexler's Sunday puzzle keeps solvers moving in both directions.
articles.content:

articles.title: Velloni focused on hybrid future, not manual gearboxes
articles.description: The sports car maker admits some buyers still want a manual, but says its priority is refining its new hybrid drivetrain.
articles.content:
Sports car maker Velloni says it has no plans to bring back a manual gearbox, even though some loyal customers keep asking for one.
The brand's engineering chief, Luca Fenwright, said development money was going into its new hybrid drivetrain instead.
"We hear the requests, and we understand the emotion behind them," he said at a media event.
"But the performance and emissions targets we have set mean the hybrid system comes first."
Velloni's current range uses an eight-speed dual-clutch transmission paired with an electric motor.
Fenwright did not rule out a manual for a future special edition, saying such projects are often reserved for limited-run models.

articles.title: Corvane (CRVN) Unveils Auto And Edge AI Push At Developer Summit
articles.description:
Corvane used its annual developer summit to show new automotive and edge AI chips.
Management described plans to run AI assistants directly in vehicles and home devices.
The firm also announced new laptop design wins.
These announcements...
articles.content:
Corvane used its annual developer summit to show new chips for cars and connected devices.
Management said the company wants its processors to become the default computing layer for in-car assistants.
The firm also announced two new laptop design wins with mid-sized manufacturers.
What it means for investors
The automotive business is still small, contributing less than a tenth of revenue.
Analysts expect it to grow faster than the rest of the company over the next three years.
Risks
Car makers take years to adopt new chips, so revenue from these deals may arrive slowly.
Competition from larger chip designers remains intense.
This article is general in nature and is not financial advice.
